Anatomical features
How the model is built
  • Bones, articular cartilage (femoral, tibial, patellar), patella and the ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL come from the MRI segmentation of cadaver specimen S193761 (Dryad, CC0). The left knee was mirrored to a right knee. Shading uses ambient occlusion baked from the real geometry.
  • The patella rotates 0.7° per degree of knee flexion about the transepicondylar axis and is then pushed onto the trochlea so it keeps the cartilage contact seen in the MRI; it is for orientation only and does not enter any calculation.
  • The lateral and medial epicondyles are the most prominent points of each condyle; the flexion axis passes through both (transepicondylar axis).
  • Default kinematics are the passive flexion path of this knee recorded on a 6-degree-of-freedom robot (Dynamics Data, PFLEX, mean of 3 trials): tibial internal rotation and anterior/medial-lateral translation, applied in Grood–Suntay convention (translations in the tibial frame). Data cover 0–70°; values are held constant beyond 70°. No parameter is fitted, so every row of the literature check is out of sample.
  • The alternative coupled mode adds tibial internal rotation in proportion to flexion, fitted to Helito 2014; this knee actually rotates far less on the robot.
  • The teaching panel also shows this knee's measured internal rotation at 5 N·m (IE laxity tests), for comparison with the population model.
  • The colour surface scans (femur, patella, tibia with menisci) were registered to the MRI model by trimmed iterative closest point (median surface distance about 1.5 mm for femur and patella); they are for display only.
  • Grafts are straight lines; an optional via-point deep to the proximal quarter of the LCL models the usual LET route. Agreement with Kittl 2015 depends on this choice: a via-point at mid-LCL does not reproduce it.
  • Fixation points are projected onto the bone surface. Femoral ALL origin follows Kennedy 2015 (4.7 mm proximal, 2.8 mm posterior to the lateral epicondyle).
  • Tibial insertion: Vietnamese cadaver measurements (16.0 mm from Gerdy, 15.8 mm from fibular head) and Claes 2013 (21.6 and 23.2 mm). The relative position between the two landmarks is nearly identical (50% vs 48%); only absolute distances differ. In this specimen the Gerdy–fibular head distance is 51.6 mm, so the Vietnamese ratio point lies 26.0 mm from Gerdy.
  • The iliotibial band and Kaplan fibers are not in the MRI and are drawn schematically.
  • Vietnamese anatomy (default for planning): ALL origin distance, insertion position, ALL and ITB dimensions and anatomical features come from a cadaver study of 22 Vietnamese knees (formalin-fixed, caliper measurements; repeat readings showed SEM 0.9° for rotation). The origin direction was not recorded, so the app places it at the most isometric point on the measured-distance ring.
  • Fractures (Segond, tibial spine avulsion types I–III) are simulated by cutting a fragment of adjustable size from this knee's tibia at the ALL or ACL footprint and displacing it; they illustrate typical patterns and are not derived from a patient scan. A displaced fragment disables the ligament attached to it; an undisplaced or fixed fragment does not.
  • Patient scan: DICOM files are parsed in the browser (uncompressed transfer syntaxes), grouped by series, sorted by slice position and converted to millimetre patient coordinates. A similarity transform (with mirroring for left knees) fitted to four user-placed landmarks maps the scan onto the 3D knee.
  • Planning extras: femoral tunnel convergence is checked as the closest distance between a 9 mm ACL tunnel (footprint to lateral cortex) and a 5 × 25 mm ALL socket; indication flags restate the STABILITY trial inclusion profile (Getgood 2020) and expert-consensus factors (Sonnery-Cottet 2017; Getgood 2019); tibial slope is measured from four user-placed points.
  • Fixation is drawn as a typical example, not a recommendation: ALLR as a free tendon graft with a femoral interference screw and a tibial suture anchor; modified Lemaire LET as an ITB strip left attached at Gerdy, passed deep to the LCL and stapled to the femur. Implant choice does not change the length calculations.
  • In Teaching mode, internal rotation under 5 N·m comes from the virtual-knee model (Geeslin 2018, Lee 2023, Noyes 2017, Delaloye 2020).
  • In fixed-axis mode, points on the axis are isometric; points proximal to it tighten in extension and slacken in flexion (Krackow principle). Real flexion axes vary between knees, so the map is indicative only.
  • For geometric illustration and decision support; not clinically validated.
